analysis:
The only change in this PR is one documentation row added at head line 414 of docs/reference/configuration.md. It documents `DARKBLOOM_TTFT_GDN_BLOCKED`, a Gated DeltaNet prompt-window kernel selector for qwen3_5, qwen3_5_moe and prism_hadamard_qwen35. The head excerpt starts at line 1 but is truncated before line 414, so the new row itself is visible only in the patch excerpt, and that excerpt is also cut off. The base unit covers lines 519 onward, which is unrelated to the changed line. I could not read the full row or any implementation.

The documented behavior is: the default probe keeps a four-row kernel only where it is bit-identical to `gated_delta_step`. Forced `packed` or `rows` kernels skip that check and are for A/B measurement only. Decode, MTP verification and masked updates use the stock kernel. The variable is read once per process and is not forwarded to LaunchAgents.

Security view: this is a documentation-only change and alters no code, so there is no regression in the documented controls. The variable is process-local and not passed through the LaunchAgent allowlist, so it does not reach installed daemons. An operator forcing a kernel affects only their own provider's computation. That matches existing threats T-007 and ADV-001, where a malicious provider can already serve manipulated outputs, and it adds no new trust boundary crossing. Nothing touches A-001, A-003, attestation, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or prefix cache storage (T-041).

Open question: the actual `GatedDelta.swift` kernel change, if present in this PR, is outside the supplied evidence. Whether the probe really guarantees bit-exact output cannot be verified from the docs alone. The platform integrator should check that no source change in the full PR affects the correctness or memory safety of the Metal kernel.
